source.title: Mapping the boundary of latent planning

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates no-CoT performance on multi-step planning tasks, a behavioral test of latent planning that uses task accuracy rather than the original hidden-state measurements or interventions.
record.gate_note: The study measures success on prompted, synthetic planning tasks, not future-token representations or causal effects on intervening text. It does not test rhyme planning, token decodability, or pre-caching. Figure-only horizon values are not extracted. Results cited from other work, including AISI and BashArena, are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study measures no-CoT, single-forward-pass accuracy on multi-step planning tasks, plus a matched-pair test of whether the first action accounts for later costs. This is behavioral evidence bearing on V5 (latent look-ahead beyond verse). It has no probes or interventions on internal representations, so it shows capability, not mechanism.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also stress that the benchmark cannot distinguish failures of state tracking from failures of search or representation.
record.recipe_differences: Measures accuracy on prompted, synthetic multi-step planning tasks with single-integer outputs; it does not probe or intervene on hidden representations or future-token features.
record.method_sensitivity: Planning accuracy varies with horizon. For GPT-6 Astra, repeating the prompt or adding filler tokens improves performance; exact per-condition values are not stated.

fits_no_version.finding: Task-specific RL (LoRA, 120 updates) raised Kimi K2.6 no-CoT held-out accuracy from 5.2% to 19.3%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Latent planning ability can be increased by direct training on no-CoT planning tasks.

record.problems: The study does not inspect representations or intervene on them, and explicitly says its benchmark does not distinguish failures of state tracking from failures of search or representation. The tasks are synthetic and less naturalistic than interactive planning. Many condition-specific values are presented in figures without numbers in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No separate numerical rows for individual horizons or for GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 horizon curves: the supplied text gives no per-model, per-horizon values. Figure 5’s exact values for prompt repetition and filler-token conditions are also not stated. The cited AISI and BashArena results were excluded because they are not results of this study.

untested.parts: Internal representations of future steps (probing, interventions), chess, Sokoban, non-transformer architectures.
Whether success comes from heuristics rather than plans is only partly addressed: tasks are verified non-greedy-solvable, but there is no mechanistic test.

missing.what: Matched-pair first-action control set: older models usually chose the cheapest immediate action, while newer models accounted for later costs more often. No numbers are given. This is the most direct look-ahead test in the study.
missing.locator: Astra shifts the boundary of latent planning, paragraph after Figure 4

missing.what: For Sol and earlier models, prompt repetition and filler gave only modest gains limited to shallower horizons.
missing.locator: Searching for an upper bound on latent capabilities; Figure 5

record.verdict_notes: Treated as a behavioral (T2) test of V5. A stricter reading, where V5 requires evidence about internal representations, would class this as fits_no_version. The answer is a single integer, so no future output tokens are planned; the look-ahead is over task steps within one forward pass. The AISI and BashArena figures are cited from other work and are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Rhyme-word representations and interventions on rhyming verse.
Decodability of tokens several positions ahead from a single hidden state.
Whether features are computed early because they help later positions rather than as a side effect.
Rhyme planning in open-weight models, including attribution-graph or probing tests.
The study tests no-CoT planning behavior on synthetic graph, grid, and dungeon tasks, but does not inspect internal representations or test chess, Sokoban, or other architectures.
Whether apparent plans arise from local next-token features or heuristics rather than representations that steer generation.
